title: Add authoritative shipment tracking fields to Container Booking
description: Close the audited container logistics-tracking gap by adding persisted shipment tracking fields to the existing Container Booking as the authoritative record and exposing them read-only from linked pre-loading or loading workflows. Repository schema code and non-production test validation are allowed. Do not call carriers, customs, freight forwarders or external tracking systems; do not execute production SQL, backfill historical shipments, deploy, or release.
acceptance_criteria: Container Booking create, edit, list and detail workflows support optional shipment mode (LCL or FCL), bill-of-lading number, shipping-order number, destination port, transit port, ETD, ETA, ATD, ATA and trucker name.

An optional customs-broker reference reuses active BaseOtherInfo entries whose InfoType is CustomsBroker, stores a validated name snapshot, rejects arbitrary authoritative free text, and preserves readable historical snapshots when the dictionary entry later becomes unavailable.

Inspection requirement is stored as an explicit nullable value so unknown, not required and required are distinct; inspection date and customs-release date remain optional and are never inferred from free text.
Linked pre-loading and loading-list detail workflows display the authoritative Container Booking tracking values without copying or independently editing a second conflicting tracking record.
When no persisted authoritative booking link or tracking value exists, the UI displays unknown or unavailable rather than matching by container number or other free text.
Existing bookings and linked documents remain readable without production backfill, and no historical departure, arrival, inspection or release date is invented.
No save operation automatically mutates freight-forwarder, customs, expense, Trade Document or inventory records and no external tracking request is made.
Repository schema changes are idempotent and validated only through permitted local or test-database paths; production database execution remains behind the mandatory human gate.

Unit/integration tests cover LCL/FCL, optional dates, customs-broker validation and historical snapshot behavior, authoritative linked display, missing-link behavior and non-mutation of adjacent modules; safe validation passes.
Browser/UI acceptance is recorded as deferred during development according to project policy.

scenarios: Edit a Container Booking with FCL mode, B/L and SO numbers, ports, schedule dates and an active CustomsBroker dictionary entry, then verify the values persist in list and detail views.
Open an authoritatively linked loading workflow and verify it shows the Booking tracking values read-only; open an unlinked record and verify no text-based linkage or invented tracking value appears.

human_gate.reason: Repository shipment-tracking code and non-production test schema only. Production database changes, external carrier/customs integrations, deployment and release require separate human approval.
